facts.text: Landers sits in the Mojave Desert and was the epicenter of the 1992 Landers earthquake, a 7.4 magnitude strike‑slip event that shook the high desert.
The community’s unofficial nickname, “Landroids,” nods to the UFO lore surrounding Giant Rock and the Integratron, built by George Van Tassel from 1957 to 1977.
Giant Rock, a seven‑story granite boulder covering 5,800 square feet, hosted Van Tassel’s flying‑saucer conventions that drew thousands in the 1950s and 1960s.
Landers hosts two major amateur astronomy sites: Goat Mountain Astronomical Research Station and the Center for Solar System Studies, the latter featuring a USGS seismic station.
The town’s post office, now home to the Morongo Basin Historical Society, preserves early 20th‑century mining history that began with Charles Reche’s 1914 gold search on Goat Mountain.
Gubler Orchids, started in 1954 by Hans Gubler, has grown into a third‑generation family business that still sells orchids from a storefront in Landers.
